summary: LTP and Quote clients on one NSE equity: the Quote client moves the subscription up (a PUT of the LTP code, a POST of 1501), and a 1105 text event (t:1_2885,110:...,119:...) becomes, on the desktop, a Quote tick that serves both.

notes: 1105 carries the touchline codes 110-119 (families/xts/binary.rs parse_1105); it has no MessageCode and no trade time.
The Jainam web client marks it 1512 and its adapter publishes it to every mode the symbol's subscriptions hold, with the quantities as floats (audit FB-05).

The desktop holds one subscription per instrument at the highest mode its clients ask for (websocket::manager), so the Quote client changes the LTP subscription into a Quote one; the web adapter subscribes each mode on its own.

deviations.reason: The web's XTS LTP data carries the last traded quantity as ltq; the desktop's LTP frames carry no last quantity (audit C06 carrier, lane wire).

The event carries no trade time: the web sends 0, the desktop the time it received the event (feed::bridge::ltt). A receipt time is not a trade time (rules: no invented data): the XTS feed should mark the trade time absent (QuoteField::LastTradeTime) so ltt is left out.
data.mode is the label every broker's frames carry on the desktop (ltp, quote, full), as the recorded Zerodha transcripts carry it; this web adapter puts its subscription mode number there.
The web parses the 1105 text values with float(), so it sends the quantity last_quantity as a float; the desktop sends a whole quantity, as for every other XTS event.
